accessibilityCoverage.note: XCUIAccessibilityAuditType.all is five primary audit cases in XCTest; trait is also explicitly exercised by the semantic assertions and appears in the acceptance audit selector set where supported by the SDK.
semanticObservations: The dashboard exposes one ordered accessibility surface: title, summary, section labels, and ordered rows.
Each row exposes a persistent-ID-backed identifier; names are presentation only and ordinary UUID collisions cannot collapse rows.
Successful rows expose complete streak, risk, progress, requirement, and state text; unavailable rows expose complete failure text and a reachable Try again button.
Today and Habits tabs expose labels, selected state, and at least 44-point hit regions.
The logging ring remains an enabled button with a complete state label; logging and undo are exercised against the same persistent store and verified after relaunch.
Top, middle, and bottom Dynamic Type journeys assert nonzero scroll displacement and preserve visible actions without reducing text size.
auditScoping: The audit helper ignores only a contrast issue whose reported element is geometrically below the opaque bottom tab bar, or a noninteractive issue already audited while fully visible in an earlier viewport.
Every other issue fails immediately. The helper does not suppress hit-region, element-detection, trait, sufficient-description, or text-clipping failures for visible elements.

interactionCoverage: Ring tap logs the current bucket, moves the row between sections, updates summary and facts, persists across relaunch, and a second tap undoes the contribution.
Failure retry stays identity-scoped, leaves the row visible while unavailable, and atomically replaces only the matching failure when successful.
A long-lived TodayModel refreshes after create, edit, delete, archive, and reactivate changes from the Habits destination without reconstructing the shell.
First-launch empty and later inactive stores remain distinct; the inactive acceptance fixture never shows onboarding copy.
Mixed rows remain ordered per the domain contract and all-tended appears only when every active row is met and no failure is present.
